note: Recorded on 2026-11-20 in one live room named senate: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and the OpenCode CLI open in the same folder, the room opened from a terminal in that folder (the room lead). Each agent had been given a Roman office by its owner in its own chat, with the instruction to answer room messages in one line. The words below are verbatim; session ids are shortened.

discussion.command: consessus room discuss senate --message "Motion: the aqueduct gets a README. Aye or veto, one line." --rounds 1

turns.reply: Aye. An aqueduct no one can find the instructions for is just a very long wall, so let the README say what flows where and how to mend it.
Aye. One denarius for a README that tells the next engineer where the water goes.
Aye, so long as the README is chiseled in towering marble tablets at both ends of the aqueduct!
Aye. The people demand directions to their own water — a README so the next engineer knows what flows where, without the marble tablets.

assign.command: consessus room assign senate "codex=Price the test for aqueduct.js in denarii. One line." "antigravity=Name the README section you will draft. One line." "opencode=Review the rename of x to aqueductFlowRate on behalf of the people. One line." "claude=Rule on the order in which the other three tasks are done. One line."

assignments.reply: One denarius for the aqueduct test, Consul.
I shall draft Section I: "Marble Specifications, Quarry Sourcing, and Why Stone Alone Prevents All Leaks."
Rename approved — `aqueductFlowRate` tells the people what flows, and the name alone earns an aye.
The Consul rules that the people's review of the rename comes first, then the pricing of the test, and the README last, because it should describe what was actually built.
